memory_candidates.content: In jq, `EXPR as $x | BODY` produces ZERO outputs entirely (BODY never runs) when EXPR is a generator that yields zero values (`empty`), not `null`. To implement a fallback-on-no-match composed from a predicate that returns `empty` on no hit (e.g. scopes_overlap_first), convert its result to `null` first via `[EXPR] | first`, then branch on `!= null` before falling back to a second call. This is the same idiom self_mod_match already uses in file-scope-overlap.sh for the identical reason, and is the correct general pattern whenever one jq def must compose a fallback around another def whose convention is `first // empty`.

orchestrate-batch-admit.sh (and other scripts guarded by deploy-root-guard.sh) refuses to run directly from the agent-system source-store path with a loud ERROR demanding a deployed .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ tree (two levels under root). To probe such a script ad hoc outside its existing test suite, copy the production script plus its lib/ dependencies (file-scope-overlap.sh, common.sh, task-lookup-lib.sh, deploy-root-guard.sh, task-lock.sh) into a throwaway temp root shaped like a deployed tree, mirroring the pattern test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh itself already uses, rather than trying to invoke the source-store copy directly.

sapience_notes.subject: jq as-binding over an empty-producing generator
sapience_notes.value: EXPR as $x | BODY in jq produces zero outputs entirely (never runs BODY) when EXPR is a generator yielding zero values (empty), not null. To compose a fallback around a predicate that returns empty on no-hit, convert its result to null first via [EXPR] | first, then branch on != null -- the idiom self_mod_match already uses in file-scope-overlap.sh for the same reason.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-batch-admit.sh deploy-root-guard refusal
sapience_notes.value: orchestrate-batch-admit.sh refuses to run directly from the agent-system source-store path, erroring via deploy-root-guard.sh's requirement for a deployed .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ tree two levels under root. Ad hoc probing requires copying the production script plus its lib dependencies into an isolated temp root shaped like a deployed tree.

sapience_notes.subject: sentinel-vs-sentinel masking fix locus in orchestrate-batch-admit.sh
sapience_notes.value: In orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's $overlaps comprehension, the SAME per-peer scopes_overlap_first call site decides both which peer collides ($hit) and which defer_reason label fires downstream (file_scope_collision vs whole_tree_claim, decided purely by testing $hit.ov_path == whole_tree_claim_sentinel). Giving a concrete-path overlap precedence over the reserved sentinel therefore required swapping only that one call site to a precedence-wrapper def; the downstream branching logic needed zero changes.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh .claude-extensions.json diff size
sapience_notes.value: Running deploy-headless.sh regenerates .claude-extensions.json's per-extension merged_sections/data_skeleton_files bookkeeping in full even when only two scripts under one extension changed, producing a large line-level diff (~1800 changed lines in one observed run) that is expected and not evidence anything else was touched. Verify a redeploy by diffing the actual deployed scripts against the source store, not by eyeballing the registry diff.

sapience_notes.subject: shared .claude-extensions.json regeneration target under concurrent dispatch
sapience_notes.value: In a multi-agent /orchestrate batch, .claude-extensions.json is a shared regeneration target: it can already show as modified in git status before a given dispatch's own deploy runs, from a sibling dispatch's concurrent deploy. git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check (scoped to the task's own declared file_scope) is what keeps a phase commit from either silently dropping a legitimately-declared shared file or sweeping in unrelated foreign changes to files outside file_scope.
